name: AI Query Optimisation
title: AI Query Optimisation
answer: Query optimisers choose how a database executes a query, picking join orders, access paths and algorithms. Research and commercial systems now use machine learning to estimate costs, recommend indexes and tune settings automatically. The aim is faster queries and less manual tuning. The risk is that a learned choice is hard to explain when it goes wrong, which makes debugging and trust harder.

Research and commercial systems now use machine learning to estimate costs, recommend indexes and tune settings automatically. The aim is faster queries and less manual tuning. The risk is that a learned choice is hard to explain when it goes wrong, which makes debugging and trust harder.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: Learned query optimisation runs alongside the database engine, often as a component of the query planner or as an external service. It depends on query logs, execution statistics, schema metadata and sometimes hardware counters as training data. The models themselves may run on the same server, on a separate CPU or GPU, or in a managed cloud service. Many teams prototype on PostgreSQL, which is a common open source base, and the site itself is built from a PostgreSQL database.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The work starts with collecting representative queries and their actual execution costs. Models are trained to predict cardinality, select join orders, recommend indexes or tune configuration knobs. Common approaches include regression, neural networks and reinforcement learning, with evaluation on benchmarks and held out production workloads. Because a learned plan can be wrong, teams often keep a traditional optimiser as a fallback and compare plans before switching.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Query logs and execution traces often contain sensitive values, so provenance and access control matter before any model training. Teams need to know which queries trained a model, how the model version maps to a plan, and who can change it. When a learned choice causes a regression, the ability to explain and roll back is a practical requirement, not just a research goal. Licensing and data use terms for third party training data also need review.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction is toward tighter integration with AI assistants and agents that write and run SQL. The site tracks 263 Model Context Protocol servers for SQL databases and warehouses, which suggests a growing layer where AI systems reach databases directly. In that setting, query optimisation may become a service that agents call, with learned components suggesting plans, indexes and settings. The open questions are how to keep those suggestions explainable, auditable and safe when they touch production systems.
